signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: NZD/JPY faces strong downside momentum as the G10 scorecard flags JPY outperformance against NZD weakness, yielding a 2.315% weekly spread across G10 pairs. Spot trades at 90.09, showing severe undervaluation with a BEER model z-score of −3.29σ against model fair value at 93.82. RBNZ policy rate sits at 2.75% while BoJ sits at 1.0%, but sustained JPY buying and high domestic inflation expectations (+2.70%) continue to support JPY strength across all cross-currency pairs. Positioning shows NZD net short of −23,004 contracts (4th percentile) while JPY net short sits at −111,297 contracts (2nd percentile), pointing to extreme short-covering pressure in JPY. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY, driven by broad G10 currency divergence. Catalyst: BoJ rate decision on 18 Sep — market bias hawkish. Risk: Sharp risk-on rebound that restores higher-yielding carry demand.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Retail Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 153.78, holding below its SMA20/50/200 moving average cluster at 158.45/160.16/158.43. Saxo 25-delta risk reversals show a pronounced put skew of −2.31, indicating institutional demand for downside protection despite a 275bp Fed-BoJ policy rate spread (Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0%). Retail sentiment sits at an extreme 86% long, directly diverging from institutional options hedging and Leveraged Funds CFTC net short of −111,297 contracts (2nd percentile, z=−2.18). VRP is negative at −0.6% (IV 10.8% vs HV30 11.3%), reflecting a potential vol mean-reversion setup as downside pressure accelerates. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, contrarian to retail long extreme and aligned with options downside skew. Catalyst: US CPI release on 12 Sep. Risk: Fed-BoJ 267bp SOFR-TONA OIS carry differential asserts dominance and halts short-covering.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7216, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.7151/0.7054/0.6995. Leveraged Funds positioning shows AUD net long at +50,250 contracts, sitting at the 94th percentile of its 52-week range (z=+1.79), indicating crowded institutional long exposure. Retail sentiment is extremely stretched at 91% short, establishing a strong institutional-versus-retail divergence. RBA policy rate at 4.35% vs Fed 3.75% provides a +60bp carry advantage (+70bp on AONIA-SOFR OIS basis), which combines with a positive Economic Surprise Index of +17.3 to support the bullish trend. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; crowded institutional positioning caps near-term expansion speed. Catalyst: US Core CPI on 12 Sep. Risk: Sudden drop in commodity prices that undermines the AUD real yield advantage.

signals.title: EUR/USD — ECB Rate Decision + Technical Alignment
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1627, anchored between its SMA20 (1.1619) and SMA200 (1.1638). The ECB maintains policy rate at 2.4% against Fed 3.75%, leaving a 135bp rate differential (+146bp on SOFR-€STR OIS basis) favoring USD, though market expectations lean toward a hawkish ECB stance. Leveraged Funds remain net short at −52,784 contracts (31st percentile), while retail sentiment shows 64% short positioning. Option volatility sits in a balanced regime with 1M ATM IV at 5.0% against HV30 of 4.6% (VRP +0.4%), reflecting low market fear ahead of central bank events. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD; interest rate differential caps structural upside. Catalyst: ECB Rate Decision and Press Conference on 10 Sep. Risk: Hawkish ECB forward guidance triggers short-covering toward SMA200 resistance.
